text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty ALERT: DNS_PROPAGATION_FAILURE fired for service `api.redwood.ai` — sudden spike in 502/524 from edge in EU region. Paging: @ryan (oncall)

ryan (oncall): Acked. I'm online. Looking now. Any recent deploys? :eyes:

pagerduty: ryan (oncall) acknowledged the alert (incident #PD-4821). Escalation timer paused.

ryan (oncall): quick status: Grafana shows 502 rate up ~7% of requests for eu-west-1 starting ~08:11Z. Latency ok for successful requests. Error body looks like upstream TLS/connection problems on LB.

ash (eng-oncall): I'm next to check infra. @sam, can you verify target health on the EU ALB/NLB?

sam (netops): on it. I see ALB eu-west-1 listener 443 has 2/4 targets healthy. Health check failures mostly `ssl handshake` and `connection reset`. No recent autoscaling events.

ash (eng-oncall): running curl to loadbalancer (from eu vm):

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health
* About to connect() to api.redwood.ai port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 18.204.11.123...
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (18.204.11.123) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error:
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'api.redwood.ai'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'api.redwood.ai'
```

elaine (support): Support queue: several customers in EU reporting intermittent 502s since ~08:12Z. Skipped SLAs: brief but visible spike.

sam (netops): Checking Route53 records and recent changes. No Route53 record change in last 24h but I do see a weighted record set where weight for eu endpoints was adjusted yesterday (manual rollout). TTL currently 300s.

ash (eng-oncall): Could be a mis-provisioned cert on a subset of backend hosts combined with weights causing traffic to go to those targets. Any cert rotations yesterday?

sam (netops): ops-runbook shows a cert replacement on the canary ALB listener yesterday at ~02:14Z. I pulled the listener config: one target group still references the old AMI that didn't get cert re-deploy.

maya (sre-lead): If some targets have mismatched certs, SNI mismatch could cause the handshake error seen. We need to reduce customer impact quickly: options — (A) shift Route53 weight away from the failing target group, (B) drain/taint failing targets, (C) rollback listener change. Which is fastest?

ryan (oncall): I'm going to shift Route53 weight to secondary region and set TTL to 60s temporarily. @sam can you prepare the change?

sam (netops): Preparing Route53 change. Proposed JSON change (short):

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12ABC --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-primary","Weight":10,"AliasTarget":{...}}},{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"global-fallback","Weight":90,"AliasTarget":{...}}}]}'
```

sam (netops): Also setting `TTL=60` for the record. Applying now.

incident-bot: Change submitted to Route53 (change-id: /change/C0ABC123). Status: PENDING.

ash (eng-oncall): I'm going to drain the suspect target group in eu-west-1 so new connections don't hit cert-mismatched hosts. Draining target-group tg-0a1b2c3d.

ash (eng-oncall): Drain started. Health checks show remaining targets stabilizing.

pagerduty: incident updated: route53 weight change applied, on-call actions in progress.

sam (netops): Route53 change INSYNC now. Verified via `dig` from multiple public resolvers:

```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
52.17.44.11
3.121.78.9
```

sam (netops): Some caches still resolving to old IPs due to upstream resolver caches, but majority now hitting fallback.

elaine (support): Error rate dropping. Tickets show 502s decreasing over the last 5 minutes.

ash (eng-oncall): TLS errors on curl gone for fallback IPs. Re-tested health endpoint: OK.

maya (sre-lead): Good. Continue monitoring 15m. Post-incident actions: identify why cert roll didn't apply to that target group and why weighted routing sent significant traffic to it.

anna (cto): Heads-up: notify enterprise customers in EU about brief degradation. Keep message factual: duration, regions, mitigation.

ryan (oncall): Incident timeline so far:
- 08:11Z alert fired (PagerDuty) — 502 spike EU
- 08:13Z ack + initial triage
- 08:18Z identified ALB target TLS handshake failures
- 08:22Z Route53 weight change + TTL reduction submitted
- 08:25Z Route53 change in-sync, fallback traffic active
- 08:27Z drains started on suspect target group
- 08:32Z error rate returned to baseline

maya (sre-lead): Customer impact: elevated 502s for approx 21 minutes, mostly EU region. Estimated affected request volume: ~7% of EU traffic during the window. No data loss. Severity: Sev2.

elaine (support): Posting status update to status.redwood.ai and sending an email to impacted customers now.

ash (eng-oncall): Root cause hypothesis: partial certificate replacement and a subsequent weighted DNS configuration that routed more traffic to partially-updated targets.

sam (netops): Follow-ups I will do: audit listener deploy script, add canary verification to cert rotation, update runbook for weighted DNS changes.

ryan (oncall): Handoff: I need to step out for 20m at 09:05Z — @ash will stay on follow-up. Leaving a note in incident tracker.

ash (eng-oncall): I'll own the follow-up and postmortem. Scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 09:30Z.

incident-bot: Incident closed by ryan (oncall). Final state: mitigated, monitoring. Incident duration: ~21 minutes.

maya (sre-lead): Thanks team. Please add all commands and console screenshots to the incident doc. We'll include a checklist item to lower default DNS TTL for weighted rollouts in the runbook.

anna (cto): Appreciate the quick mitigation.

ryan (oncall): Adding timeline + impact numbers to the ticket now.

elaine (support): Status page updated. Customer emails sent. Marking support action items done. :white_check_mark:

sam (netops): Adding change to infra backlog for improved deploy checks.

ash (eng-oncall): Closing thread after postmortem draft posted.
